text:
Jake Guentzel is on a heater: CBS Sports counted ten points in five games through Thursday's win in Columbus, including a four-assist night against Buffalo. He has 24 points in 20 games, and the Lightning have dominated with him on the ice, holding 62.8% of the expected goals (the share of quality chances) at five on five.

Some of this is going to come back. He has 11 goals on 8.45 expected and is shooting 20%, above his 17% last season and above the top of our range for him. Tampa has also scored 8.5 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of on-ice luck that fades. None of that makes him a fraud: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the front of the net at an 81st percentile rate last season, and he lives off the cross-slot passes that go in far more often than shots a player makes on his own. His ice time has also jumped two minutes a night over his last ten games. The role is real; the finishing rate is the part we'd expect to cool.
